llm.summary: This stock-analysis skill is not clearly malicious, but it automatically saves and uploads generated financial reports and uses broad agent-routing and persistence instructions that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill uses external market-data APIs, environment-supplied tokens, local Obsidian paths, cache files, and Baidu Netdisk authorization through bypy; these are partly relevant to the workflow but not tightly scoped or consent-gated.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The documented fallback installation clones the current czsc repository or installs the latest package without pinning, and the reviewed code contains a hard-coded Tushare API token.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares highest-priority activation for broad stock-analysis phrases, assigns a mandatory trading-expert role, requires actionable long/short strategies, and instructs future analyses to obey user-confirmed knowledge-base updates.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Reports, charts, K-line caches, and user-confirmed conclusions are retained across runs, and reports/charts are uploaded to cloud storage automatically when bypy is authenticated.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Chan-theory market-analysis purpose generally matches market data fetching, charting, and report generation, but the package also includes automatic local Obsidian writes, Baidu Netdisk uploads, bypy subprocess use, and persistent knowledge-update behavior that exceed a simple analysis skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill reading market-data credentials, writing reports/charts locally, using an existing bypy Baidu Netdisk authorization, and uploading generated analysis artifacts automatically. Prefer disabling or removing cloud upload and persistent knowledge updates, rotating the exposed Tushare token, and pinning dependencies before use.
llm.findings:
[P2] unexpected: The REPORT_SAMPLE.md occurrences are zero-width characters embedded in ordinary Chinese report text; I did not find hidden role-change or override instructions there, so this signal is downgraded.
[TP4] expected: Token-backed market-data API use is disclosed and coherent for live market analysis, but it contributes to the broader data-handling risk when combined with local persistence and cloud sync.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad triggers and highest-priority activation language are artifact-backed and can route generic stock-analysis requests into this skill without a narrow user intent signal.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Automatic local saves and Baidu Netdisk uploads are disclosed in SKILL.md and implemented in scripts, but they are not presented as opt-in per run.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The scripts upload generated reports and charts to Baidu Netdisk using bypy, which is a high-impact external transfer for user-derived financial research.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Subprocess-based bypy commands are used for cloud listing, upload, and related workflows; this is broader authority than core chart rendering or analysis requires.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The skill explicitly asks the agent to update a dynamic knowledge base with user-confirmed conclusions and follow them later, without an approval or rollback boundary.
[E1] expected: The itick.org outbound API call and ITICK_TOKEN use are expected for XAUUSD live-data retrieval and are documented, though still sensitive configuration.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill relies on file writes, external APIs, subprocess execution, local paths, and cloud credentials without a clear least-privilege boundary.
[T01] unexpected: The static finding is supported by the highest-priority routing and mandatory role instructions in SKILL.md.
[T02] unexpected: The persistent knowledge-base update instruction is present in SKILL.md and repeated later in the file.
[T09] unexpected: The hard-coded Tushare token in scripts/chan_czsc.py is artifact-backed and should be treated as an exposed credential.
[T08] unexpected: The install instructions use mutable, unpinned git and pip sources for czsc, which can change after review.
